rows.selection_reason: No experiments have been completed yet, so the main uncertainty is the baseline performance of the simplest RNA-only pipeline. This experiment tests a minimal, low-complexity reference: single-profile RNA with PCA, without image, aggregation, or fusion. It is the best next use of budget because it establishes an anchor for later comparisons of RNA encoders, profile settings, image modality, and multimodal fusion while changing as few design choices as possible.

Existing evidence is sparse: only config_001 (RNA-only, single-profile PCA) has been run, with modest accuracy 0.485 and F1 0.464, so it is still unclear whether image features carry useful signal. config_010 tests an image-only, single-profile ResNet50 baseline, isolating the image modality/representation without introducing fusion, multiprofile aggregation, or a new RNA encoder. This is the best next use of budget because it establishes a second unimodal anchor, clarifies whether multimodal fusion is worth pursuing, and avoids assuming that adding modalities or complexity will help.

The completed experiments show a strong RNA-only baseline (config_001, acc 0.485, F1 0.464) but a weak image-only ResNet50 baseline (config_010, acc 0.208, F1 0.172). The key uncertainty is whether the image modality is intrinsically uninformative or simply poorly represented by ResNet50. config_013 tests a stronger image encoder, ImageNet ViT-L, while keeping the same image-only singleprofile setting, so it isolates the effect of image representation. This is the best next experiment because it determines whether an image branch is worth combining in multimodal models before spending limited budget on more complex fusion or multiprofile variants.

RNA-only PCA single-profile is clearly stronger than either image-only model (0.485 vs 0.208/0.227), so the most promising direction is improving the RNA branch. The key uncertainty is whether multiprofile aggregation adds value over the single-profile baseline. config_002 keeps the same PCA encoder and uses the simplest multiprofile aggregation (avgpool), isolating the profile/aggregation effect before testing transformer or multimodal fusion. It is a logical, low-complexity extension of the best completed experiment and will tell whether profile aggregation is worth further investment.

Existing evidence shows RNA-only multiprofile with avgpool substantially outperforms RNA-only singleprofile (0.591 vs 0.485 accuracy, with similar F1 support), while image-only models are much weaker. This experiment tests whether transformer aggregation improves over avgpool for the same promising RNA multiprofile setup, isolating the aggregation choice. It is the best next use of budget because it directly extends the strongest observed direction and reduces uncertainty about the best RNA aggregation before investing in more complex multimodal configurations.

Existing evidence shows RNA multiprofile with avgpool is the strongest setting so far (accuracy 0.591, F1 0.573), while transformer aggregation is weaker and image-only models are weak (accuracy ~0.21-0.23). The key uncertainty is whether a learned RNA representation can improve on PCA in this best profile/aggregation setting. config_008 keeps the proven multiprofile + avgpool design and changes only the RNA encoder to scgpt, testing whether a pretrained single-cell foundation model adds useful signal. This is the best next experiment because it exploits the strongest RNA direction, isolates the representation choice, and either produces a stronger base model or confirms PCA before spending budget on multimodal fusion.

The strongest completed result is RNA-only multiprofile PCA with avgpool (config_002, 0.591 acc), while image-only models are weak, with ViT-L slightly better than ResNet50. The key uncertainty is whether image features add complementary signal to the best RNA-only setup. config_024 tests this directly by adding the strongest image encoder to the best RNA profile/aggregation using simple concat fusion, keeping other settings aligned with the current best RNA-only model. This is the most informative next step because it gives the image modality its best chance while still providing a clear comparison to config_002.

The strongest completed result is config_024, a multimodal multiprofile model using PCA, ViT-L, avgpool, and concat, with validation accuracy 0.6287 and F1 0.5993, clearly above the RNA-only PCA avgpool baseline of 0.5907. The main untested factor in this promising setup is fusion type. config_025 changes only fusion from concat to weighted, keeping the otherwise best-known representation, profile setting, and aggregation. This isolates the effect of fusion, is a direct exploitation of the current best direction, and has high expected performance while reducing uncertainty about whether weighted fusion can improve further.

The strongest result so far is config_025, a multimodal multiprofile model using PCA, ViT, avgpool, and weighted fusion. RNA-only evidence shows PCA with avgpool is strong, but scGPT has only been tested in RNA-only mode, where it underperformed PCA. It is therefore unclear whether a learned RNA encoder can help in the best multimodal setting. config_049 changes only the RNA encoder from PCA to scGPT while keeping the promising multiprofile, ViT, avgpool, and weighted fusion settings fixed, cleanly isolating the RNA representation effect. This is a high-value next experiment because it either identifies a better RNA encoder for the current best pipeline or confirms PCA as the preferred RNA representation under a limited budget.

The strongest result is config_025 (multimodal multiprofile PCA + ViT, avgpool, weighted fusion; 0.635 acc, 0.618 F1). Avgpool outperformed transformer in RNA-only multiprofile PCA, but aggregation has not been tested in the best multimodal setting. config_027 changes only aggregation to transformer while keeping the promising RNA encoder, image encoder, profile setting, and weighted fusion fixed, directly testing whether transformer aggregation can improve the current best. This is a one-factor extension of the most promising direction and efficiently resolves whether avgpool is optimal before further exploration.
